Prices, quantities and revenue along a demand curve

Source: R/market.R
demand_curve_values.Rd

Prices, quantities and revenue along a demand curve

Usage

price_at(d, q, ...)

quantity_at(d, p, ...)

marginal_revenue(d, q, ...)

elasticity(d, q, ...)

consumer_surplus(d, q, ...)

Arguments

d

A demand object from linear_demand() or demand_fn().

q

Quantity. May be a vector.

...

Passed on to methods.

p

Price. May be a vector.

Value

A numeric vector.

  • price_at() – the price at which q is demanded (inverse demand).

  • quantity_at() – the quantity demanded at price p.

  • marginal_revenue() – \(P(q) + q P'(q)\), the extra revenue from one more unit when the price must fall to sell it.

  • elasticity() – the price elasticity of demand at q, \((dQ/dP)(P/Q)\); negative, and below \(-1\) where demand is elastic.

  • consumer_surplus() – the area under the demand curve and above the price, up to q.

Examples

d <- linear_demand(intercept = 100, slope = 1)
price_at(d, c(0, 40, 100))
#> [1] 100  60   0
quantity_at(d, 60)
#> [1] 40
marginal_revenue(d, 40)      # 100 - 2 * 40
#> [1] 20
elasticity(d, c(20, 50, 80)) # elastic above the midpoint
#> [1] -4.00 -1.00 -0.25
consumer_surplus(d, 40)
#> [1] 800
